## FileBondExerciseNoticeStore

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.CashFlow.FileBondExerciseNoticeStore</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/CashFlow/FileBondExerciseNoticeStore.cs:14](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/CashFlow/FileBondExerciseNoticeStore.cs#L14).

Governed exercise-notice evidence: one write-once JSON record per notice under the security, a single decision by a different actor, and verification that a selected scenario exercise restates exactly what an approved notice says. Nothing here posts a redemption. Writers hold an in-process gate and a per-notice lock file, so two hosts sharing the storage root cannot both record under one identity or decide the same notice twice.

Governed corporate-action accounting lane. Attaches the durable exact-version projection binding from the retained Asset Accounting Event Spine Drafted candidate, records maker-checker approval, and executes posting through the spine&#x27;s posting authority — the only route to immutable journals and posted lot effects. Every command fails closed with a typed problem code when scope, policy coverage, period posture, balanced journals, lot resolution, retained evidence, or the required maker-checker approval is missing, and a failed attempt leaves the case recoverable in its prior state.

Fans out to every registered ICorporateActionProvider for mastered symbols, normalizes announcements, computes cross-provider consensus over full economic value keys, and records every distinct observation in the durable proposal inbox. Provider agreement is retained as evidence and never appends or approves accounting by itself. The legacy append path remains only for hosts/tests that have not registered durable operations.

## CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.CorporateActions.CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/CorporateActions/CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate.cs:98](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/CorporateActions/CorporateActionScopeFanOutGate.cs#L98).

Default gate over IAuthoritativeScopeFanOutService. Two conditions must both hold before a decision is applied, and they are separate questions. First, the affected set must be known: a non-authoritative fan-out is a refusal, never an empty affected set. Second, the known set must be applicable in one command: the durable acceptance path opens exactly one case in one serializable transaction, so a fact reaching several scopes cannot be applied without leaving the remainder un-cased. Refusing the multi-scope case is what keeps &quot;apply the decision atomically&quot; true rather than aspirational; lifting it is store work, not endpoint work. A fact reaching a scope the caller does not own is refused for the same reason and one more: the caller may not decide on another tenant&#x27;s behalf, and telling them the scope exists would itself be a cross-tenant disclosure. The refusal states that the fan-out is not confined to the caller&#x27;s own scope without naming the others.

Resolves the superseded action&#x27;s downstream impact (via the trust snapshot), maps the impacted fund to its durable ledger books, and delegates to IPeriodAwareRestatementResolver with a SecurityMasterRevisionPublishedEvent shaped as: RevisionId = superseding CorpActId, EffectiveFrom = superseded ExDate, ChangedFields = &#91;&quot;corporateActions.&lt;CanonicalName&gt;&quot;&#93;. ## IAffectedLedgerBookResolver

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.IAffectedLedgerBookResolver</code>. Kind: `interface`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/IAffectedLedgerBookResolver.cs:19](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/IAffectedLedgerBookResolver.cs#L19).

Resolves the durable accounting ledger books a published Security Master revision could have touched, so the period-aware restatement resolver (Phase 3) can route each book by its accounting period lock status. This is the publish-time feed for SecurityMasterRevisionPublishedEvent.AffectedLedgerBookIds; without it the resolver is a no-op end-to-end (an empty affected-book set short-circuits to no restatement). Restatement protects durable accounting books — the only ledger surface that carries an accounting-period lock. Those books are keyed by fund profile, so a fund-scoped impact resolves to that fund&#x27;s books. When the impact reports no ledger exposure, or no durable ledger backend is configured, there is no locked book to protect and the affected set is empty.

## IPeriodAwareRestatementResolver

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Application.SecurityMaster.IPeriodAwareRestatementResolver</code>. Kind: `interface`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/IPeriodAwareRestatementResolver.cs:21](../../../../src/Meridian.Application/SecurityMaster/IPeriodAwareRestatementResolver.cs#L21).

Phase 3 period-aware propagation: decides, for a published Security Master revision, whether any affected ledger book is in a closed period and therefore requires a governed restatement proposal rather than silent mutation. The authoritative lock state is the ledger accounting-period status (ILedgerPeriodLockReader) — the same authority LedgerPeriodPostingGuard enforces. Routing per book (D3 matrix): Open → immediate propagation (lower-order publish handlers already applied it), no restatement; SoftClosed → the downstream effect posts as a governed adjustment (a later slice), and only already-published report packs become restatement candidates; HardClosed or any indeterminate/default-deny state → no posting and a mandatory restatement proposal. When a hard-closed book has exposure but no candidate can be located, the decision still reports SecurityMasterRestatementDecision.RestatementRequired (a manual &quot;locate affected packs&quot; task) — a closed period is never silently completed.
